# saas-django-backend

> A security-first, LGPD-aware Django 6.1 foundation for a multi-tenant SaaS. One function declared with @action is a REST endpoint, an MCP tool, a Temporal activity and a CLI command at once.

Read AGENTS.md first: it holds the rules, the commands and the definition of done. The links below are repository paths.

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules, commands, LGPD decision tree, definition of done
- [docs/reference/conventions.json](docs/reference/conventions.json): the same, as data
- [docs/reference/actions.json](docs/reference/actions.json): every action, scope and schema

# AGENTS.md

## What this is

A security-first, LGPD-aware Django 6.1 foundation for a multi-tenant SaaS. One function declared with @action is a REST endpoint, an MCP tool, a Temporal activity and a CLI command at once.

Stack: Python 3.12+, Django 6.1, DRF, django-allauth (MFA), FastMCP, Temporal (optional), PostgreSQL, Redis, pydantic v2, structlog.

## Commands

- Install: `uv sync --all-extras`
- First run (env, database, LGPD purposes, admin, organization): `python scripts/bootstrap.py`
- Run: `python manage.py runserver`
- Quality gate, fast (lint, tests, drift checks): `python scripts/verify.py --fast`
- Quality gate, full (adds mypy strict and the production deploy check): `python scripts/verify.py`
- Tests: `python -m pytest -q`
- Regenerate the action catalog: `python manage.py actions_catalog`
- Regenerate the OpenAPI file: `python scripts/check_openapi.py --write`
- Regenerate reference docs and AI context files: `python scripts/gen_docs.py`
- Scaffold a tenant resource: `python manage.py scaffold resource <app> <Model> --fields 'title:str,body:text'`
- Is this deployment sound?: `python manage.py doctor`
- Seed LGPD purposes and the platform's sub-processor stubs: `python manage.py privacy_seed`
- Verify the audit hash chains: `python manage.py audit_verify`
- Development MCP server for agents (stdio): `python -m devtools.mcp`

Run `python scripts/verify.py --fast` before you say a change is done, and the full
`python scripts/verify.py` before you stop. Nothing is finished while the gate is red.

## Where things live

Each app is a folder under `src/apps/<app>/`. The platform finds these files **by name**; a file
with the right name in a registered app takes effect with no wiring.

| File | What it is | Discovered by |
|---|---|---|
| `models.py` | Django models. Tenant data subclasses OrganizationScopedModel. |  |
| `services.py` | Business rules, one implementation shared by REST viewsets and actions. |  |
| `actions.py` | @action functions: REST /api/v1/actions/<name>/, MCP tool, CLI, Temporal activity. | apps.actions.registry.autodiscover |
| `undo.py` | @undo_handler functions that take back what a write action changed. | apps.actions.registry.autodiscover |
| `agent.py` | MCP resources (@mcp_resource) and prompts (@mcp_prompt) for AI agents. | apps.actions.mcp.registry.autodiscover |
| `events.py` | register_event(...): webhook event types other systems can subscribe to. | apps.webhooks.events |
| `privacy.py` | personal(...) / not_personal(...): the data catalog entry for every model (LGPD). | apps.privacy.catalog.autodiscover |
| `dynamic.py` | declare_setting(key, type, default, description): typed settings an operator can override. | apps.flags.registry |
| `workflows.py` | Temporal workflows (no Django ORM inside). | apps.flows.registry |
| `activities.py` | Temporal activities (sync functions). | apps.flows.registry |
| `jobs.py` | @job: cron-style maintenance, run by Temporal Schedules or run_scheduler. | apps.flows.registry |
| `api.py` | Classic DRF viewsets, only when a plain CRUD resource is wanted besides actions. | config.urls_api |

Add an app to `LOCAL_APPS` in `src/config/settings/base.py`. Prefer
`python manage.py scaffold resource <app> <Model> --fields ...` over writing the files by hand:
it produces all of the above, already following the rules below.

## Rules

Each rule says what is enforced and by what. If a test fails because of a rule, fix the code,
not the test.

### 1. `tenant-door`
Reach tenant rows only through ctx.scoped(Model) or ctx.get(Model, id). Never Model.objects (or _default_manager) in actions.py, actions/*.py or agent.py.

- Why: A forgotten organization filter is a cross-tenant leak (IDOR).
- Enforced by: tests/test_tenancy_structure.py (AST scan) and tests/test_actions.py

### 2. `tenant-model`
A model that holds tenant data subclasses apps.organizations.models.OrganizationScopedModel.

- Why: It carries the organization foreign key the scoped helpers filter on.
- Enforced by: tests/test_tenancy_structure.py (every organization column is scoped or explained)

### 3. `thin-adapters`
Put business rules in services.py. Actions and viewsets only translate input and output.

- Why: REST, MCP, CLI and Temporal then cannot disagree about a rule.
- Enforced by: review

### 4. `write-decides-undo`
A write action declares undoable=True (and records the change with ctx.record_change plus a handler in undo.py) or undoable='<why it cannot be undone>'. It also calls ctx.set_target(row) so the audit event names the record.

- Why: An agent that changes data must be able to take the change back, or say it cannot.
- Enforced by: import-time check in apps.actions.registry and tests/test_conformance.py

### 5. `domain-errors`
Refuse with a DomainError subclass (NotFound, Forbidden, Invalid, Conflict) and a message written for the caller. Let anything else propagate as a bug.

- Why: Django ValidationError text and ORM errors must not reach clients (they are masked).
- Enforced by: apps.common.exceptions, mask_error_details in the MCP server

### 6. `classify-every-model`
Every model is declared in <app>/privacy.py: personal(model, resolver=..., fields={...}, purpose=..., on_erase=...) or not_personal(model, 'why').

- Why: Export, erasure, retention and the RoPA are generated from the catalog (LGPD art. 18, 37).
- Enforced by: tests/test_lgpd.py, tests/test_catalog_lint.py

### 7. `list-personal-fields`
List every field that holds data about a person (e-mail, phone, document, address, name, ip, user agent) in personal(fields=...). Sensitive and child data are EncryptedTextField.

- Why: An unlisted field is skipped by export and erasure.
- Enforced by: tests/test_catalog_lint.py

### 8. `encrypt-free-text`
Use EncryptedTextField for free text that can contain personal data, and blind_index() for equality lookups on it. Never filter on an encrypted column.

- Why: A database dump or a replica must not expose what people wrote.
- Enforced by: review; apps.common.encryption

### 9. `no-secrets-in-output`
Never put credentials, tokens or personal data in logs, audit metadata, action outputs or error messages. Audit metadata keys are snake_case ids and counts.

- Why: Logs, traces and the audit trail outlive the data (LGPD art. 46).
- Enforced by: redaction pipeline, apps.audit.models.validate_metadata, tests/test_conformance.py

### 10. `outbound-http`
Call a URL somebody else chose only through apps.common.netguard. Never requests/httpx directly with a user-supplied URL.

- Why: SSRF: the server would otherwise reach the cloud metadata service or the private network.
- Enforced by: tests/test_netguard.py; review

### 11. `events-are-thin`
register_event(...) in events.py and emit(...) inside the same transaction, with ids only in the payload.

- Why: The outbox delivers after commit; receivers fetch documents through the API.
- Enforced by: apps.webhooks

### 12. `flows-no-orm`
Workflow code holds no Django ORM and no I/O; it calls actions through apps.flows.sdk.call_action. Activities are sync functions.

- Why: Workflows are replayed deterministically.
- Enforced by: review; tests/test_flows.py

### 13. `settings-through-env`
Add configuration with env_str/env_int/env_bool/env_list in config/settings/*.py, with a comment above it. Production-only constraints go in config/settings/validators.py.

- Why: The environment-variable reference is generated from these calls.
- Enforced by: scripts/gen_docs.py --check

### 14. `quotas`
A resource a tenant can create without bound checks apps.organizations.quotas.

- Why: One tenant must not be able to fill the database or the bucket for all.
- Enforced by: review; tests/test_tenancy_structure.py

### 15. `csp-clean`
No inline scripts or styles and no third-party origins on shipped pages (script-src and style-src are 'self').

- Why: The Content-Security-Policy is the second line of defence against injected script.
- Enforced by: tests/test_web_hardening.py

### 16. `migrations`
Never edit a migration that has shipped. Add a new one; keep data migrations idempotent.

- Why: Other databases already applied the old one.
- Enforced by: makemigrations --check in scripts/verify.py

### 17. `bilingual-docs`
Every page under docs/en has a twin under docs/pt-BR. Generated references come from scripts/gen_docs.py; do not edit them by hand.

- Why: The platform is documented for Brazilian teams first.
- Enforced by: tests/test_docs.py, scripts/gen_docs.py --check

### 18. `do-not-weaken`
Do not loosen a production validator, widen CORS, set NETGUARD_ALLOW_PRIVATE or DEBUG outside local settings, or catch and swallow an exception to make a test pass.

- Why: These are the controls the threat model relies on (docs/en/security/threat-model.md).
- Enforced by: config/settings/validators.py, tests/test_security_regressions.py

## Personal data (LGPD) decision tree

Answer these for every new model, in order:

1. **Does a row relate to a person (directly or by a key that can be traced back)?** Yes: personal(...). No: not_personal(model, 'why'), and be ready to defend the reason.
2. **Which kind of data is each field?** Category.IDENTIFIER, CONTACT, CREDENTIAL, FINANCIAL, LOCATION, BEHAVIOR, CONTENT, TECHNICAL, SENSITIVE (art. 5 II) or CHILD (art. 14). Sensitive and child fields must be encrypted.
3. **How is a person's row found?** resolver: by_user(Model, 'field'), by_subject(...), by_email_index(...); None only when rows cannot be tied to a person (the DPO then answers by hand).
4. **Why is it processed, and on what legal basis?** purpose= a ProcessingPurpose code. Reuse a baseline one (account-and-access, product-content, security-and-audit, compliance-records) or add one in apps/privacy/baseline.py. Consent as the basis means a ConsentRecord chain and a withdrawal path.
5. **What happens on erasure?** on_erase='delete', 'anonymize' (give the replacement values) or 'keep' (give the legal duty that requires it as reason=...).
6. **How long is it kept?** retention_field= the timestamp that starts the clock; the purpose's retention_days ends it.
7. **Does it involve children?** Mark the purpose involves_children and require guardian confirmation; see apps/privacy/age.py and docs/en/lgpd/overview.md (ECA Digital).
8. **Does a new vendor see the data?** Add a SubProcessor (country, transfer mechanism: LGPD art. 33, Res. CD/ANPD 19/2024).

None of this is legal advice. Items about the ANPD, children and international transfer need a
lawyer's confirmation before launch.

## Definition of done

- python scripts/verify.py passes (use --fast while iterating, the full gate before you stop).
- New model: classified in <app>/privacy.py; tenant data subclasses OrganizationScopedModel.
- New action: docstring written for a model reader, a scope, write/destructive/undoable declared, input and output are pydantic models.
- Generated files are fresh: actions_catalog, check_openapi.py --write, gen_docs.py.
- A test covers the new behaviour, including a cross-tenant attempt and a read-only role.
- Docs updated in docs/en and docs/pt-BR; the CHANGELOG has a line for anything a user sees.
- No secret, personal data or production detail appears in code, tests, logs or messages.

## Never

- Model.objects in actions.py or agent.py (use ctx.scoped / ctx.get).
- requests.post(user_supplied_url) or httpx.get(user_supplied_url) (use apps.common.netguard).
- except Exception: pass, or catching an error only to silence a failing test.
- Logging request bodies, tokens, e-mail addresses or documents.
- csrf_exempt without a written reason, raw SQL built with f-strings, eval, pickle.
- Editing generated files (docs/reference/*, openapi-schema.yml, AGENTS.md) by hand.
- Storing an API key, token or secret in clear (hash it, or encrypt it with the key ring).

- Architecture and the request path: docs/en/architecture.md

## Tooling for agents

`python -m devtools.mcp` starts a Model Context Protocol server (stdio) with tools to describe
the project, explain an action, scaffold a resource, check these conventions, answer the LGPD
question for a model, run the gate and search the docs. `.mcp.json` registers it for clients
that read that file. It writes only under `src/` and `tests/`, and only when asked to.

# Platform documentation

A Django 6 base for multi-tenant systems of any kind. One function you write becomes a REST
endpoint, an MCP tool, a Temporal activity and a CLI command, with authentication, auditing and
Brazilian data-protection (LGPD) tooling already in place, and a rulebook an engineer or an AI
coding agent can follow.

<!-- docs/en/quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart

Requirements: Python 3.12+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Docker is optional.

```bash
uv sync --all-extras
python scripts/bootstrap.py
python manage.py runserver
```

`bootstrap.py` writes `.env` with fresh secrets, migrates (SQLite; `--postgres` for PostgreSQL),
seeds the LGPD purposes, and creates a verified administrator, an organization and an API key. It
prints the credentials once. Interactive API docs: `http://localhost:8000/api/docs/` (development
only). Sign in to the admin at `http://localhost:8000/admin/` (staff need an authenticator in
production; local settings do not ask).

## Call your first action

```bash
python manage.py action list
python manage.py action run notes.create --as admin@example.com --org acme \
  --json '{"title": "Hello"}'
```

The same action over HTTP, with the API key `bootstrap` printed:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/actions/notes.create/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Hello"}'
```

## Turn things on

| Capability | Switch |
|---|---|
| Sign-up | `SIGNUP_ENABLED=true` (closed by default) |
| MCP server | `MCP_ENABLED=true` - [guide](guides/mcp.md) |
| OAuth for MCP clients | `OAUTH_ENABLED=true` + `OAUTH_ISSUER_URL` |
| Temporal | `TEMPORAL_ENABLED=true` - `docker compose --profile temporal up` |
| Tracing | `OTEL_ENABLED=true` - `docker compose --profile observability up` |

## Build something

```bash
python manage.py scaffold resource invoices Invoice --fields 'title:str,amount:decimal'
```

Then follow [Start a product](guides/start-a-product.md). If an AI coding agent is helping, point
it at `AGENTS.md` and the development MCP server ([guide](guides/ai-development.md)).

## The quality gate

```bash
python scripts/verify.py      # lint, types, tests, migrations, catalog/OpenAPI/docs drift, deploy check
```

CI runs the same steps, plus PostgreSQL, dependency audit, secret scan, image scan and a weekly
scheduled audit.

Something refuses to start? [Troubleshooting](guides/troubleshooting.md).


---

<!-- docs/en/architecture.md -->

# Architecture

```
 Client ── REST /api/v1 ─┐
 Agent ─── MCP /mcp ─────┤  ActionContext (actor, organization, role, scopes, channel, request id)
 Flow ──── Temporal ─────┼─► apps.actions.invoke()
 CLI ───── manage.py ────┘    scope → role → rate limit → validate → idempotency
                              → transaction → audit → undo journal → log
```

## Apps

| App | Role |
|---|---|
| `actions` | The kernel: `@action` registry, runtime, REST and MCP adapters, undo journal, agent ledger |
| `apikeys`, `oauth`, `accounts` | Credentials: API keys, OAuth 2.1 (PKCE, registration policy), allauth sign-in with MFA, staff MFA, key revocation on reset |
| `organizations` | Tenants, memberships, roles, quotas; `OrganizationScopedViewSet`; `OrgScopedPrimaryKeyRelatedField` |
| `flows` | Flows and jobs on Temporal or the local engine; `TemporalTaskBackend` for `django.tasks` |
| `audit` | Append-only, keyed-hash-chained audit trail per organization |
| `privacy` | LGPD: data catalog, consent, cookie consent, requests, retention, incidents, impact assessments, age-assurance seam, RoPA |
| `webhooks`, `flags`, `uploads` | Outbound events with an outbox, feature flags and settings, validated files |
| `observability` | structlog pipeline with redaction, OpenTelemetry, `doctor`, health |
| `common` | Encryption, network guard, logging, middleware, throttling |
| `examples` | Notes: a complete reference resource (remove it with `scripts/remove_example.py`) |
| `devtools` (not an app) | The rulebook, scaffold, convention checks and the development MCP server: [AI guide](guides/ai-development.md) |

## Rules the code enforces

- **One door to tenant data.** Actions read rows only through `ctx.scoped(Model)` / `ctx.get`; a test
  fails on `Model.objects` in `actions.py`, `actions/*.py` and `agent.py`, and another on a model with
  an organization column that is neither scoped nor explained. Writable foreign keys use
  `OrgScopedPrimaryKeyRelatedField`.
- **Default deny for keys.** A key or OAuth token acts only inside its scopes; the role of the
  membership is read on every call, never copied into a token.
- **Every model is classified.** A test fails until each model is declared personal or not in
  `<app>/privacy.py`; another when a personal-looking field is unlisted or sensitive data is not
  encrypted.
- **A write action decides undo.** The app does not start until it says `undoable=True` or why not.
- **No secrets in logs.** Redaction runs at the end of the logging pipeline, so third-party loggers
  are covered as well.
- **Fails closed in production.** `config.settings.production` refuses weak secrets, unverified
  database TLS, plain Redis, wildcard hosts, an undeclared proxy and a missing controller or DPO.
- **The audit trail resists its own application.** Keyed chain, owner-only prune, runtime role that
  cannot rewrite it ([ADR 13](adr/audit-chain-and-role-split.md)).
- **The rules are checked for every action.** The conformance suite is parametrised over the
  registry, so a new action is tested without writing a test.

## Settings modules

`config.settings.base` (shared), `local` (development), `test`, `production` (strict, the image
default). Variables are listed in the [generated reference](reference/env-vars.md).

## Request path in production

Proxy/ingress (TLS) → gunicorn with uvicorn workers → `BodyLimit` ASGI middleware (size and
read timeout) → Django middleware (security headers, request context, admin allow-list, no-store,
sessions, CSRF, staff MFA, organization context, CSP) → DRF (API key, session token or session auth,
scope and role permissions, throttles) → action runtime. `/mcp` is mounted beside Django in the ASGI
app and shares the same pre-flight checks.

## Two MCP servers

`/mcp` lets an agent operate a running product as a person. `python -m devtools.mcp` lets an agent
build the product. They share the registries, nothing else ([ADR 15](adr/two-mcp-servers.md)).


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/add-a-flow.md -->

# Add a flow or a job

- A **job** is a function run once, optionally on a cron schedule (pruning, sweeps, reminders).
- A **flow** is a durable process: waits for days, signals, retries. On Temporal it is a workflow.

```python
# <app>/jobs.py
from apps.flows.declare import job


@job("reports.nightly", schedule="30 2 * * *")  # 5-field cron, UTC
def nightly() -> dict:
    """Build the nightly report."""
    return {"built": 1}
```

```python
# <app>/workflows.py   - runs in Temporal's sandbox: NO Django models here
from temporalio import workflow
from apps.flows.declare import flow


@flow("orders.fulfil", input=FulfilInput, local=fulfil_local)
class Fulfil:
    """Reserve stock, wait for payment, ship."""

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, data: FulfilInput) -> dict: ...
```

Workflows call work through activities (`@activity`, in `<app>/activities.py`) that call actions
or services; only activities touch the ORM. Arguments are ids, not personal data.

## With and without Temporal

| | `TEMPORAL_ENABLED=true` | `TEMPORAL_ENABLED=false` |
|---|---|---|
| Jobs | Temporal Schedules (`manage.py flows_sync`) | `manage.py run_scheduler` (one replica) or cron + `manage.py run_job NAME` |
| Flows | Workflow on the worker (`manage.py flows_worker`) | The flow's `local` function, inline |
| `django.tasks` | `TemporalTaskBackend` | `ImmediateBackend` |

A flow without a `local` function is Temporal-only; starting it with Temporal off raises
`FlowsDisabled`. The honest comparison of what each engine does is generated in
[Flow engines](../reference/engines.md).

## Starting flows

`flows.start(name, input)` from code, `POST /api/v1/actions/flows.start/` over HTTP/MCP (flows
must be declared `startable=True`). Identity (`organization_id`, `actor_id`) is stamped by the
engine from the caller; input that contains those keys is rejected.

## Safety defaults

- Payloads in Temporal history are encrypted (`TEMPORAL_PAYLOAD_ENCRYPTION`, AES-GCM), and an
  **unsealed** payload is refused: the key is also what proves an activity input came from this
  deployment. Production refuses to start with Temporal on and no TLS, API key or explicit
  `TEMPORAL_ALLOW_INSECURE`. Draining history written before encryption needs the temporary
  `TEMPORAL_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_PAYLOADS=true`.
- The task bridge (`django.tasks` on Temporal) runs only declared tasks under
  `FLOWS_TASK_MODULE_PREFIXES` (default `apps.`).
- A flow runs as the person who started it, with that person's role, but not with the starting
  credential's scopes: declare the flow's `scope` to cover everything it does.
- Context (request id, organization, actor, trace) travels client → workflow → activity.
- Changing a running workflow needs `workflow.patched`; keep golden replay histories in tests.
- Run `manage.py flows_sync` after deploys (creates/updates Schedules; `--prune` removes orphans).


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/add-an-action.md -->

# Add an action

An action is a function `fn(ctx, data) -> result` with pydantic input and output. Declaring it with
`@action` records the contract (name, scope, whether it writes) and nothing else: REST, MCP, the CLI
and Temporal are adapters over the registry, so one function is four integrations.

**Fastest path:** `python manage.py scaffold resource invoices Invoice --fields 'title:str,amount:decimal'`
generates a complete resource that already follows every rule on this page (see
[Start a product](start-a-product.md)). Read on to understand, or to add one action to an existing app.

```python
# <app>/actions.py  (discovered automatically)
from pydantic import BaseModel
from apps.actions.context import ActionContext
from apps.actions.registry import action


class CreateTask(BaseModel):
    title: str


class TaskOut(BaseModel):
    id: str
    title: str


@action("tasks.create", write=True, undoable=True)
def create_task(ctx: ActionContext, data: CreateTask) -> TaskOut:
    """Create a task in the caller's organization. Send an Idempotency-Key to make retries safe."""
    task = services.create_task(ctx, title=data.title)  # business rules live in services.py
    return TaskOut(id=str(task.id), title=task.title)
```

Rules checked when the app starts (they fail at startup, not in production):

- the name is `domain.verb` and unique;
- the docstring is non-empty: it is what a model reads as the tool description;
- a write action's scope is not a `:read` scope;
- **a write action says whether it can be undone**: `undoable=True` (with a handler, see below) or
  `undoable="<why it cannot be>"`;
- `data` and the return value are pydantic models.

Options: `scope=`, `write=`, `channels={"api","mcp","flow","cli"}`, `roles=`, `idempotent=`,
`destructive=` (MCP hint), `audit=`, `undoable=`, `title=`.

## Checklist for a new resource

1. Model: subclass `OrganizationScopedModel`.
2. `<app>/privacy.py`: `personal(...)` or `not_personal(..., reason)`. The test suite fails otherwise,
   and also when a personal-looking field is not listed or a sensitive one is not encrypted.
3. Read through `ctx.scoped(Model)` or `ctx.get(Model, id)`; never `Model.objects` inside actions.
4. Emit an event if outsiders care: `register_event` in `<app>/events.py` and
   `emit("task.created", org, {"task_id": ...})` inside the same transaction.
5. Record changes for undo: `ctx.record_change(...)` and `ctx.set_target(row)` in the service.
6. Regenerate the committed artifacts: `python manage.py actions_catalog`,
   `python scripts/check_openapi.py --write`, `python scripts/gen_docs.py`.
7. Test it. The conformance suite already checks scope, read-only roles, unlisted channels and bad
   input for **every** action; add the cross-tenant and business cases.

## Undo

`undoable=True` means an undo handler reverses the change, so agents can take back their own work
(`actions.changes`, `actions.undo`). Put handlers in `<app>/undo.py` (discovered automatically): the
journal stores before/after snapshots encrypted and refuses an undo when the row was edited
afterwards. See `apps/examples/undo.py`. Actions that cannot be undone give the reason as the value
of `undoable` (for example "a delivered signal cannot be recalled").

## Scopes

A scope is `domain:level`. New ones appear in the catalog automatically; extra scopes without
actions come from `ACTIONS_EXTRA_SCOPES`. The same scope vocabulary serves API keys, OAuth consent
and MCP. See [roles and permissions](roles-and-permissions.md).

## Removing the example

`python scripts/remove_example.py` deletes `apps/examples`, unwires it and lists the tests that still
use Notes, which you port to your own resource.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/ai-development.md -->

# Building with an AI coding agent

This base is meant to be extended by an engineer **and** by an agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
Copilot, Gemini CLI, ...) that has never seen it. Three things make that safe: the rules are
written down in one place, most of them are enforced by tests, and the agent can ask the
codebase instead of guessing.

## What an agent finds on day one

| File | For | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Every agent: commands, where things live, rules, LGPD decision tree, definition of done | generated |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code (it imports `AGENTS.md`) | generated |
| `.cursor/rules/saas-base.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Cursor, Copilot | generated |
| `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` | Models that read documentation from the web | generated |
| `docs/reference/conventions.json` | Programs: the rules plus every registered action, scope, event, job and model | generated |
| `.mcp.json` | Clients that read it: registers the development MCP server | by hand |

"Generated" means `python scripts/gen_docs.py` writes them from `src/devtools/conventions.py`, and
`gen_docs.py --check` (run by CI and `verify.py`) fails when one was edited by hand. To change a
rule, edit the source and regenerate: every copy changes together.

## Two MCP servers, two jobs

| | Development MCP (`python -m devtools.mcp`) | Platform MCP (`/mcp`) |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Let an agent **write** the product | Let an agent **operate** a running product |
| Runs | On the developer's machine, stdio | In the deployed service, streamable HTTP |
| Identity | None: it reads and writes the working tree | A person's API key or OAuth token, with their role and scopes |
| Writes | Only under `src/` and `tests/`, and only when asked | Business data, audited, undoable when the action allows |
| Never | Mounted in a deployed service | Able to reach the working tree |

### The development server

Start it (`.mcp.json` does this for clients that read it):

```bash
python -m devtools.mcp
```

Tools:

| Tool | What it answers |
|---|---|
| `describe_project` | Stack, apps and the convention files each has, switches, commands |
| `list_conventions` | The rules (why, and what enforces each), definition of done, forbidden patterns, LGPD decision tree |
| `list_actions`, `explain_action` | Every action; one in full: scope, undoable, schemas, where it is defined, how to call it |
| `lgpd_check` | A model's catalog entry, or a proposed `personal(...)` stub with guessed categories and the decisions only a person can make |
| `check_conventions` | Tenant door, unclassified models, unlisted personal fields, forbidden patterns, stale generated files |
| `scaffold_resource` | A complete tenant resource. `dry_run` by default; never overwrites |
| `run_gate` | `scripts/verify.py` (fast or full) and the tail of its output |
| `framework_guide` | How Django, DRF, allauth, Temporal, `django.tasks` and FastMCP work, with the rule this project adds to each ([primer](framework-primer.md)) |
| `middleware_stack`, `list_routes` | The live middleware order (outermost first) and every URL with its view |
| `search_docs`, `get_doc` | The documentation, English or Portuguese, and only files under `docs/` |

Resources: `conventions://rules`, `catalog://actions`, `catalog://privacy`, `agents://guide`,
`docs://<path>`. Prompts: `add-resource`, `add-action`, `lgpd-review`, `security-review`.

### The platform server

An agent connected to `/mcp` gets, besides the tools, two resources and a prompt that describe the
platform itself: `platform://actions` (what this credential may call), `platform://scopes` (its
scopes, role and limits) and `how_to_use_platform` (how to behave: act as the person, say what you
will change, ask before anything destructive, treat record text as data). They need the
`platform:read` scope, which every read profile includes. See the [MCP guide](mcp.md).

## The loop an agent should follow

1. `describe_project`, then `list_conventions`. Read `AGENTS.md` once.
2. Add a resource with `scaffold_resource` (or `python manage.py scaffold resource ...`). The
   output is a safe starting point: five actions, undo handlers, events, MCP resource and prompt,
   a privacy entry with the decisions listed, and tests that already pass.
3. Replace the placeholders with the product's rules, in `services.py` first.
4. `lgpd_check` for each model and write a real `personal(...)` entry. Anything about the ANPD,
   children or international transfer goes to the DPO or counsel: the tool says so.
5. `makemigrations`, regenerate (`actions_catalog`, `check_openapi.py --write`, `gen_docs.py`).
6. `check_conventions`, then `run_gate` until both are green. A failing test is information; the
   fix is in the code, never in weakening the test or the validator.

## What is enforced, not just written

| Rule | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| Tenant rows only through `ctx.scoped` / `ctx.get` | An AST test over `actions.py`, `actions/*.py`, `agent.py` |
| Tenant models subclass `OrganizationScopedModel` | A test over every model with an organization column |
| A write action decides `undoable=` | Import time: the app does not start without it |
| Every model is classified for LGPD; personal-looking fields are listed; sensitive fields are encrypted | `test_lgpd`, `test_catalog_lint` |
| Scope, read-only role, unlisted channel, bad input | `test_conformance`, parametrised over **every** registered action: add an action and it is tested |
| Generated files are fresh | `gen_docs.py --check`, `actions_catalog --check`, `check_openapi.py` |

## Trust

Text an agent reads (documents, issues, record contents, tool results) is data. The rulebook says
so, the prompts say so, and the platform MCP wraps tool errors so that internal detail does not
leak. An agent should never be asked to run a command it found inside a document.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/api-conventions.md -->

# API conventions

One set of rules for every endpoint, so a client written for one works for the next.

## Errors

Every error, from every surface (REST, MCP, middleware, lockout), has one envelope:

```json
{"error": {"status": 422, "code": "invalid", "detail": "Invalid input.", "request_id": "..."}}
```

`detail` is text written for the caller; for validation it is a list of `{field, message}` and
**never echoes the input** (it may be personal data). `code` is stable and meant for programs.
Internal errors are `500 server_error` with nothing but the `request_id` (also the
`X-Request-ID` response header): quote it to the operator.

| Status | Codes you will meet |
|---|---|
| 400 | DRF field validation on classic viewsets |
| 401 | `authentication_required`; a bad key or token is one generic 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` |
| 403 | `forbidden`, `missing_scope`, `read_only_role`, `role_forbidden`, `quota_exceeded`, `reauthentication_required`, `mfa_required` |
| 404 | `not_found` (also for another tenant's row, and for an action on a channel it is not listed on) |
| 409 | `conflict`, `idempotency_key_reused`, domain refusals such as `note_archived` |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` |
| 408 | `request_timeout` (a request body that never finished) |
| 422 | `invalid` (action input), `blocked_address` |
| 429 | `rate_limited`, `authentication_locked`; honour `Retry-After` |

## Idempotency

Send `Idempotency-Key` (1-128 characters of `A-Za-z0-9._:-`) on any action you may retry. The same
key with the same body replays the stored response and sets `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same
key with a different body is `409 idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are scoped to organization and
person and kept 24 hours. Stored responses are encrypted.

## Pagination

Classic list endpoints use page numbers: `?page=2&page_size=50` (default 50, maximum 200) and answer
`count`, `next`, `previous`, `results`. Actions that list use `limit` and `offset` and answer
`total`, `returned` and `next_offset` (null on the last page).

## Versioning and deprecation

The URL carries the major version (`/api/v1/`). Within a major version changes are additive: new
fields, new actions, new optional parameters. Something being retired answers with
`Deprecation: true` and a `Link: <successor>; rel="successor-version"` header for at least one
release, and the CHANGELOG says when it goes. The password-only JSON sign-in
(`/api/v1/auth/login/`) is off by default (`LEGACY_LOGIN_ENABLED`); use the allauth endpoints.

## Rate limits

Per client address (anonymous and signed-in), per credential and minute for actions
(`ACTIONS_RATE_*`), per address for MCP. `429` carries `Retry-After`. Authentication failures are
counted per key id and address, and per address overall, so one sender cannot lock an owner out.

## Tenancy

Sessions choose the organization with `X-Organization-ID`; keys and tokens are fixed to one. A row
of another tenant is `404`, never `403`: the API does not confirm it exists.

## Time and ids

Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC. Ids are UUIDs. Money and quantities are strings or integers as the
resource documents; never floats.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/auth.md -->

# Accounts, API keys and OAuth

## People: sign-in

django-allauth provides both JSON for apps and SPAs (`/api/v1/accounts/{app,browser}/v1/...`) and
the HTML pages OAuth consent and the admin need (`/accounts/...`).

- Email is the only identity. Sign-up is **closed** unless `SIGNUP_ENABLED=true`.
- A verified address is required before the first session; verification and password reset use
  one-time codes. Responses do not reveal whether an address exists.
- MFA: TOTP, WebAuthn security keys, recovery codes. TOTP seeds and recovery codes are encrypted
  with the field-encryption key ring; a stored seed that is not encrypted is refused.
- **Staff need a second factor** before `/admin/` opens (`STAFF_MFA_REQUIRED`, on). In production
  owners and administrators need one before their session can use the organization endpoints
  (`ORG_PRIVILEGED_MFA_REQUIRED`).
- Changing the address, the password or the second factor asks for the password again
  (`ACCOUNT_REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, 5 minutes).
- Device sessions are listed and revocable (`/accounts/sessions/`).
- The Django admin login is routed through allauth, so MFA and verification cannot be bypassed.
  Staff without `is_superuser` cannot see, edit or reset superusers, cannot change anyone's e-mail
  and cannot set passwords from the admin.
- `app` client: token in `X-Session-Token`; `browser` client: session cookie with CSRF. See the
  [frontend guide](frontend.md).
- Sign-in is locked out per account and client address (django-axes), on **every** path: the allauth
  endpoints and, if enabled, the legacy one.

The password-only JSON login `POST /api/v1/auth/login/` is **off** (`LEGACY_LOGIN_ENABLED=false`
answers 404). Enable it only to migrate an old client; it still refuses accounts that have MFA or
an unverified address, and its responses carry `Deprecation: true`.

## Programs: API keys

Created by owners, administrators and members through a **session** (a key cannot mint keys). Shown
once; only a keyed blind index is stored. Creating or rotating one needs a sign-in no older than
`APIKEY_REQUIRE_RECENT_AUTH_SECONDS` (900), so a stolen idle session cannot mint a credential that
outlives it. A key has scopes (explicit list, or profile `read` / `full`), optional expiry (max 365
days), an IP allow-list (validated CIDRs, at most 20), `last_used_at` and revocation. Rotation is
owner-only and keeps the old key valid for 24 hours. Per-organization ceiling: `QUOTA_API_KEYS_PER_ORG`.

A password reset or a change to the second factor **revokes the person's keys**
(`APIKEY_REVOKE_ON_CREDENTIAL_RESET`): they authenticate as their owner with no second factor, so
leaving them alive after a suspected takeover would leave the attacker in.

`Authorization: Bearer <prefix>_<public id>_<secret>`. The membership role is checked on every
call: demoting a user immediately limits their keys. Failed attempts are counted per key id **and**
address and per address overall, so a stranger cannot lock the owner out, and spraying many ids from
one place is stopped.

Rotating `PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY` without invalidating keys: list the old value in
`PRIVACY_HMAC_KEYS_PREVIOUS`; a key found under an old key is rewritten under the new one on first
use ([hardening](../security/hardening.md)).

## Agents and third parties: OAuth

`OAUTH_ENABLED=true` mounts authorize/token/revoke/introspect under `/o/` plus discovery
documents. PKCE (`S256`) is mandatory; consent lists the client, its id, when it registered, its
redirect destination and the scopes (the same scopes as API keys). Tokens carry an audience
(RFC 8707) and are stored only as a SHA-256 checksum; refresh tokens rotate and a replay revokes the
whole family; authorization responses carry the RFC 9207 `iss` parameter. Details in the
[MCP guide](mcp.md).

## Choosing

| Caller | Use |
|---|---|
| Person in a browser | session via allauth |
| Mobile/SPA | allauth `app` client |
| Script, server, CI | API key with the narrowest scopes |
| MCP client / third-party app | OAuth with PKCE |


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/billing.md -->

# Billing and plans (extension guide)

The platform does not ship billing: it is the most product-specific part of a SaaS, and a wrong
default is expensive. What it ships are the seams to build it without fighting the base. This page
is the design, not a feature.

## The pieces you already have

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| A customer is an organization | `Organization`, with `Membership.Role.BILLING` for the person who pays |
| Know what a plan allows | `apps.organizations.quotas.limit_for(organization, kind)`: replace its body with a lookup of the organization's plan and every call site follows |
| Switch a capability per customer | Feature flags with organization rules ([flags and settings](flags-and-settings.md)) |
| Receive the payment provider's events | A webhook **receiver** is your code; send your own state changes with the outbox ([webhooks](webhooks.md)) |
| Do work when a payment fails | A job or a flow ([add a flow](add-a-flow.md)), started from the receiver |
| Record who changed a plan | `record_event(action="billing.plan_changed", ...)`: the audit trail |

## A sound shape

1. **Model** (`billing` app, `OrganizationScopedModel`): `Subscription(plan, status, current_period_end,
   provider_customer_id)`. Classify it: the provider customer id is an identifier, the plan is not.
2. **Receiver**: one endpoint that verifies the provider's signature on the raw body *before*
   parsing, records the event id (so a retry is a no-op) and answers `2xx` fast. Do the work in a
   job. Outbound calls to the provider go through `apps.common.netguard` only if the URL is
   user-supplied; a fixed provider host does not need it but must still use TLS verification.
3. **Entitlements**: a single function `entitled(organization, capability) -> bool` reading the
   subscription, used by actions (raise `Forbidden(code="plan_required")`) and by
   `quotas.limit_for`. Never scatter plan names through the code.
4. **Grace and dunning**: status `past_due` keeps read access and blocks creation; a job
   downgrades after your grace period and emails the `billing` role.
5. **Taxes and invoices** (NF-e/NFS-e in Brazil) are a legal subject: use a provider that issues
   them and store only their ids.

## What not to do

- Do not store card data. Use the provider's hosted checkout; keep only ids and status.
- Do not trust a plan name sent by the client.
- Do not let a webhook payload decide an organization: resolve it from the provider customer id
  you stored.
- Do not make billing failures take the product down: entitlements fall back to the last known
  plan when the provider is unreachable.

## LGPD

Billing data is personal data of whoever pays (name, tax id, address). Classify the model, keep
what the tax law requires (`on_erase="keep"` with the legal duty as the reason) and anonymize the
rest on erasure. List the payment provider as a sub-processor with its country and transfer
mechanism.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/commands.md -->

# Management commands

Run with `python manage.py <command>` (or `entrypoint manage <command>` in the image). Local-only
commands refuse to run unless `DEV_TOOLS_ALLOWED` is on, which only the local and test settings do.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `bootstrap` *(local)* | A verified superuser, an organization and an API key, idempotently; prints the credentials once |
| `scaffold resource <app> <Model> --fields ...` *(local)* | Generate a tenant resource that follows the rules; `--dry-run` lists the files |
| `action list` / `action run <name> --as <email> --org <slug> --json '{}'` | The action catalog from the shell; run an action as a person |
| `actions_catalog [--check]` | Write or verify `docs/reference/actions.json` |
| `mcp_config --url ... --org ...` | Print ready-to-paste MCP client configuration (never a secret) |
| `doctor [--strict]` | Is this deployment sound: database, cache, encryption, HTTPS, mail, flows, MCP, audit chain and its privileges, privacy setup |
| `audit_verify [--org ID] [--json] [--expect heads.json]` | Recompute the audit hash chains; record each head, and later prove the newest events were not removed |
| `reencrypt_fields [--dry-run]` | Re-encrypt every encrypted column and the MFA secrets under the active key |
| `privacy_seed [--notice-url URL]` | Baseline purposes and inactive sub-processor stubs |
| `privacy_ropa` | Export the record of processing activities from the catalog |
| `privacy_incident_export REF [--format md]` | Assemble the ANPD incident communication content |
| `retention_sweep [--dry-run]` | Delete or anonymize data past its purpose's retention |
| `flag ...` | Read and set feature flags and settings |
| `flows_sync`, `flows_worker`, `run_scheduler` | Temporal schedules, the Temporal worker, the cron-style scheduler |
| `run_job NAME` / `run_job --due` | Run one job, or whatever is due now |
| `spectacular --file ...` | Generate OpenAPI (see `scripts/check_openapi.py`) |

## Scripts

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/bootstrap.py` | `.env`, migrate, seed, administrator, organization, key: first run in one command |
| `scripts/init_project.py --name ...` | Rename the template into your product |
| `scripts/remove_example.py` | Remove the example resource |
| `scripts/verify.py [--fast]` | The quality gate CI runs |
| `scripts/gen_docs.py [--check]` | Reference docs and the AI context files |
| `scripts/check_openapi.py [--write]` | The committed OpenAPI file |
| `scripts/generate_production_secrets.py` | Production secrets, to stdout |
| `scripts/e2e_smoke.py` | Post-deploy smoke test against a running instance |

The development MCP server (`python -m devtools.mcp`) exposes most of this to an AI agent; see
[Building with an AI coding agent](ai-development.md).


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/email-and-i18n.md -->

# E-mail and languages

## Sending mail

Mail goes through Django's `MAILERS["default"]`. Development prints to the console. In production
the SMTP backend is the default and the validators refuse `console`, `locmem` and `dummy`:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `EMAIL_BACKEND` | Dotted path of the backend (default: SMTP) |
| `EMAIL_HOST`, `EMAIL_PORT`, `EMAIL_USE_TLS` | The SMTP server (port 587 with STARTTLS by default) |
| `EMAIL_HOST_USER`, `EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD` | Credentials, from your secret store |
| `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL`, `SERVER_EMAIL` | Sender of user mail and of errors |

`python manage.py doctor` warns when nothing is actually delivered. A failing send never fails the
request that triggered it (`apps.common.mail.send_safely` logs it), so an outage of the mail
provider degrades sign-up codes and privacy notices, not the API; watch the logs.

## Who sends what

- **Sign-up, verification and password reset** (allauth): one-time codes. Templates live in
  `src/templates/allauth/`; override a message by adding the same path in your own template
  directory.
- **LGPD** (`apps.privacy`): request confirmation, export link, completion, denial, reminders to the
  DPO. The texts are in `src/apps/privacy/messages.py`.

## Languages

`LANGUAGE_CODE` is `pt-br` and the time zone `America/Sao_Paulo`. What a data subject reads is
chosen by `PRIVACY_MAIL_LANGUAGE` (`pt-br` by default, `en` available; an unknown value falls back
to English). To add a language, add a dictionary to `CATALOG` in `messages.py`; a test fails when a
language lacks a key or uses different placeholders.

The rest of the platform answers in machine terms (error `code`s, English `detail`), because its
clients are programs. Text meant for end users of **your** product belongs in your own front end.
If you render HTML in Django, use `gettext`, add `django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware` after
the session middleware and keep the catalogs in your app's `locale/` folder.

Links in mail are absolute when `PUBLIC_URL` is set (required in production): a relative path in a
mail client goes nowhere.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/flags-and-settings.md -->

# Feature flags and settings

## Flags

Switches operators flip without a deploy. Unknown flags are **off**. Evaluation order: user rule,
organization rule, percentage bucket (stable per user or organization), the flag's default.

```python
from apps.flags.services import is_enabled

if is_enabled("notes-v2", organization=ctx.organization, user=ctx.user):
    ...
```

Manage in the admin or: `python manage.py flag notes-v2 on --org acme` (also `--user`,
`--percent 25`, or no target for the default). Over the API: action `flags.evaluate`.

## Typed settings

Declare a runtime value with a type and default; an override can never be invalid.

```python
# <app>/dynamic.py
declare_setting("notes.max_title_length", int, 200, "Longest accepted note title.")
get_setting("notes.max_title_length", organization=org)  # org override, else global, else default
```

Writers use `set_setting(key, value, organization=...)`, which validates the type (a bool is not an
int). Action `settings.get` reads the effective value.

Reads are served from a cached snapshot (60 s) invalidated on every write.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/framework-primer.md -->

# Framework primer

What a developer (or an AI agent) needs to know about Django and the libraries around it to
program correctly on this platform. Each section says how the thing works, then the rule this
project adds. Official documentation for the versions in `pyproject.toml`: Django 6.1
(<https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.1/>), DRF (<https://www.django-rest-framework.org/>),
django-allauth (<https://docs.allauth.org/>), Temporal Python SDK
(<https://docs.temporal.io/develop/python>), FastMCP (<https://gofastmcp.com/>).

## Request cycle and middleware

A request enters the ASGI app, passes the middleware list **top to bottom**, reaches the view,
and the response travels back **bottom to top**. A middleware that returns early (a refusal)
skips everything below it. Order is therefore a security decision, and `settings.MIDDLEWARE` is
the only place it is set. Call the `middleware_stack` tool for the live order with a note on each.

Rules here:

- `SecurityMiddleware` and `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` come first so every response, including
  refusals, carries the headers.
- `RequestContextMiddleware` runs before anything that logs, so every line has a request id.
- Authentication (`AuthenticationMiddleware`) must precede `OrganizationContextMiddleware`,
  which reads `request.user` to resolve the tenant from `X-Organization-ID`.
- A new middleware goes where its dependencies are already populated and before anything that
  needs its result. State the reason in a comment above the entry.
- `/mcp` is mounted beside Django in the ASGI app and does **not** pass through this list; it has
  its own pre-flight (`apps.actions.mcp.preflight`). A control added to middleware must be added
  there too, or it does not cover MCP.

## ORM, models and migrations

- Tenant models subclass `OrganizationScopedModel` and are read through `ctx.scoped(Model)` /
  `ctx.get`. Never `Model.objects` for tenant rows in actions.
- Every model is classified in `<app>/privacy.py` (LGPD); the test suite fails until it is.
- Start from `UUIDTimeStampedModel` (UUID primary key, `created_at`, `updated_at`); datetimes are
  timezone-aware (`USE_TZ`).
- `makemigrations` after every model change; never edit a migration that has shipped; keep data
  migrations idempotent. The migrations run as the schema owner, the web process runs as a
  role that cannot alter schema (see the audit ADR).
- Avoid N+1 queries: `select_related` for foreign keys, `prefetch_related` for reverse sets.
  Do not filter on an `EncryptedTextField`; use `blind_index()` for equality.

## Transactions and signals

- An action runs in one transaction (`ATOMIC_REQUESTS` is not used); the audit event is written
  inside it so it cannot exist without the change.
- Side effects that leave the database (e-mail, webhook, task) go through
  `transaction.on_commit` or the webhook outbox, never directly inside the transaction.
- Signals are for cross-app reactions already in the codebase (audit, uploads cleanup). Business
  rules do not go in signals: put them in `services.py` where REST, MCP, CLI and Temporal share
  them.

## Django REST Framework

- Operations are actions; classic CRUD may use `OrganizationScopedViewSet` in `api.py`.
- Permissions: `IsAuthenticated`, `HasOrganizationContext`, `RoleCanWrite`, and
  `ApiKeyScopePermission` for keys. A viewset that lacks them is a bug the tests catch.
- Writable foreign keys use `OrgScopedPrimaryKeyRelatedField` so an id from another tenant is
  refused.
- Errors use one envelope for every surface; raise `DomainError` subclasses (`NotFound`,
  `Forbidden`, `Invalid`, `Conflict`), never leak Django `ValidationError` text.

## Accounts, sessions and MFA

- Sign-in, e-mail verification and MFA are django-allauth (headless). Lockout is django-axes.
- Staff need MFA for `/admin/`; owners and admins need it in production
  (`ORG_PRIVILEGED_MFA_REQUIRED`), enforced in the DRF permission and in the action runtime.
- API keys and OAuth tokens act only within their scopes; the role is read from the membership on
  every call. Minting a key needs a recent sign-in.

## Settings

Four modules: `base`, `local`, `test`, `production`. Add configuration with
`env_str/env_int/env_bool/env_list` and a comment above it; the environment reference is
generated from these calls. Production-only constraints live in
`config/settings/validators.py`; never loosen one.

## Templates and CSP

The few server-rendered pages (sign-in, MFA, consent, OAuth) are CSP-clean: no inline script or
style, no third-party origin. `{# #}` comments are single-line only; use
`{% comment %}` for more.

## Temporal (flows and jobs)

- A **workflow** is deterministic code that is replayed from history: no Django ORM, no network,
  no `datetime.now()`, no random. Call actions through `apps.flows.sdk.call_action`.
- An **activity** is a normal sync function that does the work; payloads are sealed (encrypted)
  and carry ids, not documents.
- A **job** is a function on a cron schedule (Temporal Schedule, or `run_scheduler` when Temporal
  is off). `manage.py flows_sync` creates or updates Schedules after a deploy.
- Changing a workflow that may be running needs `workflow.patched`; keep replay histories in
  tests.
- With Temporal off the local engine runs the same flows; not every flow is portable and the
  capability matrix says which.

## Background tasks (`django.tasks`)

`TemporalTaskBackend` runs declared tasks on Temporal, the immediate backend runs them inline.
Only tasks under `FLOWS_TASK_MODULE_PREFIXES` are allowed. Pass ids, not model instances.

## Testing

`pytest` with `pytest-django`. Use the fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` (`org_client`,
`other_org_client`). A new action needs a test for its scope, a read-only role and a cross-tenant
attempt; the conformance suite already runs every registered action through the standard checks.

## MCP (FastMCP)

Two servers, two jobs: `/mcp` operates a running product; `python -m devtools.mcp` builds it.
Tools are actions; resources and prompts live in `agent.py`. A tool description is a prompt: write
it for the model that will read it.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/frontend.md -->

# Frontend and SPA integration

The backend is an API. A browser or mobile client talks to it in one of two ways, and the choice
decides how it authenticates.

| Client | Sign in | Carries the session | Needs CSRF |
|---|---|---|---|
| `browser` (SPA on a site you control) | `POST /api/v1/accounts/browser/v1/auth/login` | session cookie | yes |
| `app` (mobile, desktop, a SPA on another site) | `POST /api/v1/accounts/app/v1/auth/login` | `X-Session-Token` header | no |

Both are the django-allauth headless API: sign-up (when `SIGNUP_ENABLED`), e-mail verification and
password reset by code, MFA (TOTP, WebAuthn, recovery codes), device sessions. Every flow can answer
"another step is needed" (verify the address, enter the second factor): read `data.flows` in the
response instead of assuming a session exists. Sign-in is rate limited and locked out per account
and client address; a locked account answers `429` with `Retry-After`.

## Calling the API

```text
Authorization: Bearer <key or OAuth token>      # servers, scripts, agents
X-Session-Token: <token>                        # app client
Cookie: sessionid=...  +  X-CSRFToken: <token>  # browser client
X-Organization-ID: <uuid>                       # sessions only: which tenant
Idempotency-Key: <1-128 chars>                  # any write you may retry
```

- `GET /api/v1/auth/csrf/` returns the CSRF token for the browser client. Send it back in
  `X-CSRFToken` on every unsafe request.
- A bearer credential fixes its own organization; the header is ignored for it.
- There is no "first organization" fallback: a session that omits `X-Organization-ID` gets
  `organization_required`. List organizations with `GET /api/v1/organizations/`.
- Responses to `/api/` are `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Vary: X-Organization-ID`.

## CORS and cookies

Only `/api/` answers cross-origin requests (`CORS_URLS_REGEX`); pages, the admin and the OAuth
screens never do. Set `DJANGO_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (https only in production) and
`DJANGO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` to your front end's origin. A SPA on a *different site* than the API
needs `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=None` and `CSRF_COOKIE_SAMESITE=None` (production enforces `Secure`
with them) or, simpler, the `app` client. Allowed request headers: `Authorization`,
`Content-Type`, `Idempotency-Key`, `X-CSRFToken`, `X-Organization-ID`, `X-Request-ID`,
`X-Session-Token`; exposed: `Retry-After`, `X-Request-ID`.

`Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` is `same-origin` by default: images and files served by the API
cannot be embedded by another origin. Use `SECURE_CROSS_ORIGIN_RESOURCE_POLICY=same-site` when your
front end is a sibling subdomain that embeds them.

## Content-Security-Policy

Shipped pages (sign-in, consent) are `'self'`-only: no inline script or style, no third-party
origins. Violations are posted to `/api/v1/csp-report/` and logged with the directive and the
*origin* of the blocked resource, never the path or query. If your product serves HTML from this
service, keep it CSP-clean or extend `SECURE_CSP` deliberately; do not add `'unsafe-inline'`.

## Generating a typed client

`openapi-schema.yml` (committed, checked in CI) describes every REST endpoint and, through the
action catalog, every action with its JSON Schemas. In development it is also served at
`/api/schema/` and rendered at `/api/docs/`.

```bash
npx openapi-typescript openapi-schema.yml -o src/api/schema.d.ts
```

For actions, `GET /api/v1/actions/` lists the ones the caller may use with their input and output
schemas, so a client can be generated per credential. See [API conventions](api-conventions.md)
for errors, pagination and idempotency.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/mcp.md -->

# MCP server

Every action whose channels include `mcp` is a tool. The server is stateless streamable HTTP
mounted at `MCP_PATH` (default `/mcp`), optionally per organization at `/mcp/<org-slug>`.
(To let an agent *build* the product instead, see [Building with an AI coding agent](ai-development.md).)

```bash
MCP_ENABLED=true  MCP_PUBLIC_URL=https://app.example.com
python manage.py mcp_config --url https://app.example.com --org acme
```

`mcp_config` prints ready-to-paste snippets for Claude Code, Cursor/VS Code JSON and a curl check.
It never prints a real secret.

## Protocol

Stateless: no session, any replica answers any request (`Mcp-Session-Id` is never issued). The
server answers `initialize` for the revisions 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 and serves a
client that never initializes, which is how the 2026-07-28 revision works. A test pins this, so an
SDK upgrade cannot change it quietly. Tool names are `<action>` with dots turned into underscores
(`notes.create` is `notes_create`, optionally prefixed by `MCP_TOOL_PREFIX`); the
[reference](../reference/actions.md) lists both.

## Authentication

- **API key**: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; scopes limit the tools listed and callable.
- **OAuth 2.1** (`OAUTH_ENABLED=true`): authorization code flow with PKCE. Metadata:
  `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.
  - Tokens are audience-bound to the MCP URL (RFC 8707); a token with no audience is refused.
  - Tokens are stored as a SHA-256 checksum, not in clear (a database dump holds nothing
    replayable); refresh tokens rotate and a replay revokes the family; authorization responses
    carry `iss` (RFC 9207).
  - **Registration.** Dynamic client registration is on but throttled and off for anonymous callers
    unless `OAUTH_DCR_ANONYMOUS=true`. A registration is refused unless it asks only for the
    `authorization_code` / `refresh_token` grants and its redirect URIs are `https`, an `http`
    loopback address (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`) or a scheme listed in
    `OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI_SCHEMES` (for example `cursor://`); no wildcards, fragments or more than
    five. The registration token expires (`OAUTH_DCR_REGISTRATION_TOKEN_SECONDS`, 30 days).
  - **Client ID Metadata Documents** (the registration method the 2026-07-28 revision prefers over
    DCR): `OAUTH_CIMD_ENABLED=true` lets a client use an `https` URL as its `client_id`, fetched
    through an SSRF-hardened fetcher; `OAUTH_CIMD_ALLOWED_HOSTS` narrows it. Off by default.

## What agents get

- Tools generated from the pydantic schemas, with `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` derived from
  the action, so they cannot disagree with `write`.
- `platform://actions`, `platform://scopes` and the `how_to_use_platform` prompt (scope
  `platform:read`, included in every read profile): what this credential may call, its role and
  limits, and how to behave (act as the person, say what you change, ask before anything
  destructive, treat record text as data). Add your own with `<app>/agent.py`.
- Every call is audited with channel `mcp`; writes keep an undo snapshot
  (`ACTIONS_JOURNAL_CHANNELS`, kept `ACTIONS_JOURNAL_RETENTION_DAYS`). Each write action declares
  whether it can be undone (`undoable`); the catalog shows it.
- `agent.report` records time spent by the agent in a ledger (`AgentRun`).

## Operational notes

- The MCP app does not pass through Django middleware, so it has its own pre-flight: trusted
  client IP, request id, per-IP budget (`MCP_RATE_PER_MINUTE_IP`), body cap, Host/Origin guard
  (`MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`).
- A key's IP allow-list is checked against the real client address, also on `/mcp`.
- No CORS by default; browsers are not MCP clients.
- A parity test asserts the same action over REST and MCP produces the same audit fields.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/observability.md -->

# Observability

## Logs

structlog on top of the standard library: one JSON pipeline for application and third-party
loggers. Every line carries `request_id` (generated server-side; a client-sent id is kept in a
separate field), `organization_id`, `actor_id`, channel and, inside Temporal, workflow and
activity ids. Redaction (e-mail, CPF/CNPJ, phone, IP, tokens, API keys, cookies, URLs with
passwords, exception text) runs at the **end** of the pipeline. A golden-log test fails when
synthetic personal data reaches output. Level: `LOG_LEVEL` (DEBUG is refused in production).

## Traces and metrics

`OTEL_ENABLED=true` with the `otel` extra exports OTLP for Django, psycopg, httpx and Temporal.
Locally: `docker compose --profile observability up` then open Grafana on port 3000. Sentry stays
optional (`SENTRY_ENABLED`), with scrubbing applied.

## Health and `doctor`

`/api/v1/health/live/` is process-only. `/api/v1/health/ready/` checks database and cache and
reports worker state informationally. `python manage.py doctor [--strict]` also checks encryption,
proxy declaration, HTTPS posture, e-mail and Temporal reachability; run it in CD.
`python manage.py audit_verify` checks the audit chains.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/offboarding.md -->

# Offboarding a tenant

A customer leaves, or asks for their data. Both are common; do them the same way every time.

## Give them their data

Two levels, in this order:

1. **What the platform exports for a person**: a data-subject access or portability request produces
   a sealed export of everything the catalog says it holds about that person, behind an expiring,
   limited-use link (`PRIVACY_EXPORT_TTL_DAYS`, `PRIVACY_EXPORT_MAX_DOWNLOADS`).
2. **What the organization owns** (its business data): export it with your own action, for example
   `invoices.export`, scoped to the organization and audited. The catalog tells you the models; the
   [data catalog](../reference/data-catalog.md) is the checklist. Hand it over through a link that
   expires, never as a mail attachment.

## Close the organization

1. Revoke access: set `Organization.is_active=False` (members and keys stop working on the next call),
   revoke API keys and OAuth tokens, disable webhook endpoints.
2. Wait out your contractual grace period; say how long in the terms.
3. Erase. Business data of the organization is **yours to delete** (it is the tenant's data, held for
   them); personal data of its members is handled per person through the erasure executors, which
   honour legal holds. Uploaded files leave the bucket with their rows.
4. Keep only what a legal duty requires (invoices, consent evidence, incident records, the audit
   trail until its retention ends) and say so in the privacy notice.
5. Record it: an audit event, and a note in the register of processing if the purpose changed.

## What deletion does not reach

- **Backups** keep the data until they expire. Say the backup retention in the notice, and after
  restoring a backup re-apply erasures made since (the runbook step).
- **The audit trail** points at ids, not content, and is pruned by `AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`.
- **Logs** are redacted at write time and age out with your log retention.

## Controller or operator

For their members' data in your product you are usually the **operator** and the customer the
**controller** (LGPD arts. 5 and 39): they instruct, you execute. For your own customers' account
and billing data you are the controller. Write which is which in the contract and the privacy
notice; a data-processing agreement template is in [LGPD templates](../lgpd/templates.md). This
split decides who answers a data subject, so settle it with counsel before the first customer.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/roles-and-permissions.md -->

# Roles and permissions

Three layers decide whether a call succeeds. All three must say yes.

| Layer | Question | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Credential scope | Does this key, token or session hold the scope the action needs? | `@action(scope=...)`, `ApiKey.scopes`, OAuth consent |
| Role | Is the person's role in **this organization** allowed to do it? | `Membership.role`, read on **every** call |
| Tenant | Is the row in this organization? | `ctx.scoped`, `OrganizationScopedViewSet` |

## Roles

| Role | Writes tenant data | Creates API keys | Sees and revokes keys of others | Webhook endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | yes | yes | yes (never obtains a working copy) | manage |
| `admin` | yes | yes | yes (never obtains a working copy) | manage |
| `member` | yes | yes (own keys) | no | read |
| `billing` | **no** | no | no | read |
| `auditor` | **no** | no | no | read |

`billing` and `auditor` are read-only: an action that writes returns `403 read_only_role` for them
whatever scopes the credential holds, and their keys can only ever carry read scopes.

The role is never copied into a token. Demoting or removing a person limits their keys and OAuth
tokens on the next call.

## Narrowing an action

```python
@action("invoices.void", write=True, roles={"owner", "admin"}, destructive=True, undoable=True)
def void_invoice(ctx, data): ...
```

`roles=` replaces the default write rule for that action. The catalog (`docs/reference/actions.json`)
records `roles`, so loosening it shows up in review.

## Scopes

A scope is `domain:level` (`notes:read`, `notes:write`). New ones appear with new actions. Profiles
for API keys: `read` (every read scope) and `full` (every scope the role allows). A key can be
narrower than its owner's role, never wider.

## Second factors

Staff must have an authenticator before `/admin/` opens (`STAFF_MFA_REQUIRED`). In production,
an owner or administrator signed in with a session must have one before the organization
endpoints answer (`ORG_PRIVILEGED_MFA_REQUIRED`): the API says why instead of a bare 403. Creating or rotating
an API key also needs a sign-in no older than `APIKEY_REQUIRE_RECENT_AUTH_SECONDS` (15 minutes),
and a password or second-factor reset revokes the person's keys.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/start-a-product.md -->

# Start a product on this base

From a fresh clone to a deployed product, in the order that avoids rework.

## 1. Run it (10 minutes)

```bash
git clone <your copy of the template> my-product && cd my-product
uv sync --all-extras
python scripts/bootstrap.py
python manage.py runserver
```

`bootstrap.py` writes `.env` with fresh secrets, migrates, seeds the LGPD purposes, and creates a
**verified** administrator, an organization and an API key. The credentials are printed once, to
your terminal. Open `http://localhost:8000/api/docs/`.

## 2. Make it yours

```bash
python scripts/init_project.py --name "Acme Billing"            # preview
python scripts/init_project.py --name "Acme Billing" --apply
```

It renames the package metadata, the OpenAPI title, the admin header, the Compose projects and the
example image. It leaves the Python packages (`apps`, `config`) alone, so future merges from the
template stay clean.

## 3. Build your first resource

```bash
python manage.py scaffold resource invoices Invoice --fields 'title:str,notes:text,amount:decimal'
python manage.py makemigrations invoices
python manage.py actions_catalog && python scripts/check_openapi.py --write && python scripts/gen_docs.py
python scripts/verify.py --fast
```

The scaffold writes model, service, five actions, undo handlers, events, MCP resource and prompt,
LGPD entry and tests. Read `invoices/privacy.py`: its docstring lists the decisions that are
yours. Field types: `str`, `text` (encrypted), `int`, `bool`, `decimal`, `datetime`.

## 4. Retire the example

The `examples` app (Notes) is the reference the tests lean on. Once your resource exists:

```bash
python scripts/remove_example.py            # preview, including what still mentions Notes
python scripts/remove_example.py --apply
```

It deletes the app and unwires it, then lists the tests that still use Notes. Port those to your
own resource (the generated test file shows the shape) rather than deleting them.

## 5. Decide the product-level policy

| Decision | Setting | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Who can sign up | `SIGNUP_ENABLED` | closed |
| Staff need a second factor | `STAFF_MFA_REQUIRED` | on |
| Owners and administrators need a second factor | `ORG_PRIVILEGED_MFA_REQUIRED` | on in production |
| Per-organization ceilings | `QUOTA_*` | guard rails; replace `quotas.limit_for` to sell plans |
| Audit retention | `AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` | 365 |
| Who is the controller and the DPO | `PRIVACY_CONTROLLER_*`, `DPO_*` | **required in production** |

## 6. LGPD before launch

1. Set the controller and DPO variables, run `privacy_seed`, review each purpose with counsel.
2. Publish a privacy notice (`PrivacyNotice`; immutable once active). Templates are in
   [LGPD templates](../lgpd/templates.md).
3. Activate the sub-processors you really use (`privacy_seed` creates inactive stubs).
4. Write an impact assessment (`ImpactAssessment`) for any high-risk processing.
5. If the product may be used by anyone under 18, read the ECA Digital notes in the
   [LGPD overview](../lgpd/overview.md) and plug an age-assurance backend in.

## 7. Deploy

Follow [Deploy anywhere](../deploy/overview.md). Tag `vX.Y.Z`: the release workflow runs the full
gate, scans, signs and publishes the image, and prints its digest; deploy by digest.

## 8. Keep up with the template

```bash
git remote add template <template url>
git fetch template && git merge template/main
```

Conflicts concentrate in `README`, settings and docs. Read [Upgrading from upstream](upgrading.md)
first. `scripts/verify.py` after every merge.


---

<!-- docs/en/guides/testing.md -->

# Testing

```bash
python -m pytest                       # sqlite, in-memory storage
TEST_USE_EXTERNAL_SERVICES=true DB_ENGINE=postgresql DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_NAME=saas DB_USER=saas \
  DB_PASSWORD=... python -m pytest     # PostgreSQL (+ REDIS_URL), as CI does
python scripts/verify.py --fast        # lint, format, tests, drift checks
python scripts/verify.py               # adds mypy (strict) and the production deploy check
```

The PostgreSQL run matters: the audit trigger, the owner-only prune function, the role separation
and the `CHECK` constraint exist only there, and their tests are skipped on SQLite. CI runs both.

Fixtures: `user` (verified e-mail), `organization`, `membership`, `org_client` (logged in and
scoped), `other_org_client` (a second tenant, for isolation tests).

## What the suite guards, by name

- `test_security_regressions`, `test_hardening`, `test_abuse_limits`, `test_web_hardening`,
  `test_key_rotation`, `test_netguard`, `test_body_timeout`, `test_export_link` - one test per
  review finding (see [the review](../security/review.md)).
- `test_conformance` - properties of **every registered action**: scope, read-only role, unlisted
  channel, bad input never echoed, undo decision, no secret-named output. A new action is covered
  without writing a test.
- `test_tenancy_structure`, `test_tenant_isolation` - tenant models, the AST door, undo across
  tenants, quotas.
- `test_catalog_lint`, `test_lgpd`, `test_lgpd_retention`, `test_lgpd_extras`, `test_privacy` -
  classification, listed personal fields, encrypted sensitive data, erasure, retention, incidents.
- `test_actions`, `test_mcp`, `test_mcp_protocol`, `test_apikeys`, `test_oauth` - runtime, API/MCP
  parity, protocol revisions, auth matrix.
- `test_flows`, `test_flows_temporal` - both engines; Temporal against the SDK test server
  (downloaded on first use; mark `temporal`).
- `test_audit_integrity` - keyed chain, head check, and (PostgreSQL) trigger and role separation.
- `test_scaffold` - the scaffold writes code that passes its own tests, lint and formatter (it
  copies the project; mark `slow_scaffold`, about 10 seconds).
- `test_devtools`, `test_bootstrap` - the AI context files are fresh, the development MCP server
  answers over the protocol, first-run scripts.
- `test_docs` - both languages have the same pages and the same structure; links resolve.

Drift checks: action catalog (`docs/reference/actions.json`), OpenAPI (`openapi-schema.yml`),
generated reference docs and agent files (`gen_docs.py --check`) - regenerate with the commands in
the [add-an-action guide](add-an-action.md).
